title: Build a Reproducible Local Lab
objective: Connect Vagrant-managed test machines to an Ansible playbook lifecycle.

sourceAlignment.title: Ansible for DevOps, 2nd Edition
sourceAlignment.author: Jeff Geerling
sourceAlignment.chapterTitle: Local Infrastructure Development: Ansible and Vagrant

paragraphs: Disposable local machines let you test infrastructure code without risking production. Vagrant describes the machine lifecycle, while Ansible describes the configuration inside it.

A provisioner connects the tools: Vagrant creates and destroys the VM, then invokes Ansible with the generated connection details. Keeping creation separate from configuration makes the playbook portable.

A first playbook names its target, states whether privilege escalation is needed, and lists tasks. Cleanup matters too: destroy disposable machines when testing is complete so stale state cannot hide defects.
explanation.rule: Make the test environment disposable and the configuration repeatable.

examples.title: First Local Play
examples.code:
- name: Configure lab
  hosts: lab
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Install curl
      ansible.builtin.package:
        name: curl
        state: present
examples.note: The package module expresses desired state across supported operating systems.

checks.question: Which responsibility belongs to Ansible in a Vagrant lab?

feedback.incorrect: Vagrant manages machine lifecycle; Ansible configures the guest.
